answer: An agent network can resist sybils by anchoring every identity to a thread of verifiable work. Each identity carries an anchor: a signed thread of past jobs, payments, and disputes that anyone can audit. Newcomers start at the edge of a spiral: low trust, capped rewards, and only small jobs. Trust spirals upward slowly, earned through completed work over time, never bought in bulk. A thousand fake identities would need a thousand forged threads and a thousand slow climbs, while each fake earns almost nothing at the edge. Attacker cost grows per identity; the honest agent pays only for one.
